newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fortis arranges 45.8 bln bfr funds for Pierson buy.
newsitem.headline: Fortis arranges 45.8 bln bfr funds for Pierson buy.

text.p: Belgian-Dutch banking and insurance group Fortis said on Friday it would increase own funds by 23.8 billion Belgian francs, with equal contributions coming from its two parent companies Fortis AG and Fortis AMEV.
The group will reallocate equity now tied up in various units, freeing up 14.7 billion francs and further raise debt by 7.3 billion francs.
The total, 45.8 billion francs, will pay for its recent acquisition of Dutch investment bank MeesPierson from Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV.

Fortis spokesman Corneel Maes told Reuters by telephone after a briefing for analysts earlier on Friday that the selection of debt instruments to be used would depend on market conditions and interest rate levels.

AG will pay for its share in the increase in funds for the group out of an imminent stock issue which it expects to raise some 17 billion francs. The remainder, some five billion francs, would be "funds that we might need if we were to increase our stake in ASLK Bank and ASLK Insurance. We are already calculating in the possibility," he said. Fortis is negotiating a deal to buy further ASLK shares with the Belgian government.
The group currently owns 49.9 percent in state-controlled ASLK. Fortis hopes the government will excercise a put option it holds on 9.8 percent of ASLK and sell it a further 15 percent.
Maes had no comment on how the talks were progressing.

Amev would not raise its capital to pay for its share in the new group funds. Instead, it would finance the bulk of its stake by selling assets -- in particular parts of its investment portfolio -- to the group.

In addition, Amev would transfer to the Fortis group some 231 million guilders which AG will pay to Amev as the remainder of a so-called equalisation amount agreed between AG and Amev in 1990 when the Fortis group was created.

The total sum reflected the difference in value between AG and Amev at the time of the creation of the group, with Amev being valued above AG. Maes said that the 231 million guilder transfer by AG would end the equalisation agreement early.
